title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Particulars Open to Correction and Correction Caps
content:
A correction changes a particular printed on a document of the `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` range. This page defines which printed particulars can still be changed at each stage of the document's life, how many changes a document can absorb after issue, and how far a gross weight may move after sailing.

## General clauses

1. A correction is made at the request of the documentation party. Each particular to be changed is registered as its own correction request; one request never covers two particulars.
2. Until the document is issued, any printed particular may be changed free of charge through the pre-issue revision rounds of the draft.
3. After issue and while the carrying vessel has not yet sailed, only the particulars listed for the type under "open after issue" may be changed. Once the vessel has sailed, the narrower list "open after departure" applies.
4. The shipper printed on a document is never corrected. A different shipper can be achieved only by way of a switch bill.
5. **Cap on corrections after issue.** A document accepts no more corrections after issue than the tier cap. The count is the number of correction requests on the document that were registered on or after the date of issue shown on the document record and have been completed, leaving out the request now being dealt with; that request may proceed only while this count is below the cap.
6. **Cap on consignee changes.** The consignee named on the document may be replaced after issue no more often than the tier's consignee cap. The count is the completed correction requests on the document that changed the consignee, again leaving out the request in hand. A cap of 0 means the named consignee can never be changed after issue.
7. **Weight tolerance after departure.** A gross weight corrected after the vessel sailed may move away from the printed weight by at most the tier's tolerance percentage of that printed weight. Any bigger change needs a fresh verified gross mass declaration and falls outside documentation corrections.

## Tier values

| Document type | Open after issue | Open after departure | Corrections after issue (max) | Consignee changes (max) | Weight tolerance (percent of printed weight) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | consignee, notify party, cargo description, package count, gross weight, port of discharge | consignee, notify party, cargo description, gross weight | 3 | 2 | 5 |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | consignee, notify party, cargo description, package count, gross weight, port of discharge | consignee, notify party, cargo description, gross weight | 5 | 3 | 5 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | notify party, cargo description, package count, gross weight | notify party, gross weight | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | notify party, cargo description, package count, gross weight, port of discharge | notify party, gross weight | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | notify party, cargo description, package count, gross weight, port of discharge | notify party, gross weight | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | notify party, cargo description | notify party | 1 | 0 | 2 |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- **Weight within tolerance.** An `AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading` shows a printed gross weight of 20,000.0 kg and the vessel has sailed. Three percent of 20,000.0 kg is 600.0 kg, so a corrected weight anywhere from 19,400.0 kg to 20,600.0 kg is admissible; 20,700.0 kg is not a documentation correction.
- **Cap reached.** An `AHL Straight Bill of Lading` already has two completed corrections registered after its issue. A third request cannot proceed, because the count of 2 is not below the cap of 2.
- **Particular closed.** A shipper holding an `AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading` whose vessel has sailed asks to change the cargo description. After departure that type only opens the notify party and the gross weight, so the request falls outside the list.
